title: Settings edits do not mark the scenario dirty

sections.what: The top-bar scenario chip is dirty when world._edit_seq != world._commit_seq (routes/saveload.py scenario_status). The after_request autosave hook in app.py bumped _edit_seq only for paths containing /api/graph/, /api/players/, /api/build/ or /api/world/ - so POST /api/settings/date (also clock_start, time_per_tick, forecast, forecast-override, narration, ghost_mode, mature_content) mutated scenario-persisted state (time_ticks, clock_start_hour, forecast_schedule, calendar_config, narration_mode, ghost_mode, mature_content) but never marked the world dirty. Since /api/scenario/commit just sets _commit_seq = _edit_seq, a settings edit was invisible to Commit and the user was never prompted. Fix: include the scenario-persisted settings in the dirty bump, excluding the app-global settings (engine_config, equip_slots, auto_generate_descriptions) which do not live in the scenario; a settings edit pushes no undo entry so a time-skip does not flood the undo history with 'world edit'. Verified live on a running app: clean dirty=False, POST /api/settings/engine_config stays False (excluded), POST /api/settings/date flips to True.
sections.verify:
1. GET /api/scenario/status; POST /api/settings/engine_config {values:{}}; POST /api/settings/date {}; re-GET status.
   - expected: engine_config excluded (dirty stays false); date is a scenario edit (dirty true).
   - observed (2026-10-10, live): dirty false -> engine_config 200 -> dirty false -> date 200 -> dirty true.

acceptance.text: POST /api/settings/date flips the dirty chip true (measured false -> true).

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Game menu → Settings → scenario time/date controls; top-bar
scenario chip for the dirty-state result.

Current availability: The endpoint behavior was measured live on 2026-10-10.
The click-through from Settings to the top-bar dirty chip is not recorded.

Live steps when available:
1. Load a clean committed scenario, open Settings, change the date, and save
   the setting; read the scenario chip at the top of the game view.
   - expected: the chip changes from clean to dirty because date is persisted
     in the scenario.
2. Revert or recommit the scenario, post an app-global engine-config change
   from Settings, and read the chip again.
   - expected: the chip stays clean because `engine_config` is not scenario
     content.

This section defines intended access and live acceptance. It is not a claim
that planned UI exists or works today.
